forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.headline: The committee recognises a longer-term ‘path to assurance’ on the Council’s statement of accounts.
findings.detail: The paper refers to a longer-term route to restoring assurance on the statement of accounts. It does not set out the timetable or steps in this document.
findings.matters: A stated path to assurance signals when, or whether, the council expects a clean opinion again, which lenders and peer finance teams would track.

findings.headline: The committee is asked to approve the 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, subject to minor changes, while noting the disclaimed audit opinion.
findings.detail: The Section 151 Officer's statement that the accounts give a true and fair view is relied on for approval. The Chair of the Audit, Standards and Risk Committee and the Director of Finance are to sign the Letter of Representation and the Statement of Accounts, because the external auditors provide no assurance to rely on.
findings.matters: Approval and sign-off rest on internal officer assurance rather than external audit, which is a governance position other councils facing backstop deadlines may also face.
findings.quote: The Committee approve the Statement of Accounts, shown in Appendix 2

findings.headline: Surrey Heath's 2025/26 Statement of Accounts carries a disclaimed audit opinion, which the committee is asked to note.
findings.detail: The committee is asked to note the disclaimed opinion and to recognise that it therefore provides very limited or no assurance on the statements. The paper presents this as a formal recommendation to the committee.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion means the external auditor gave no assurance on the accounts, which a finance director here or at a peer council would need to understand when judging the reliability of published figures.
findings.quote: The disclaimed opinion of the Statement of Accounts for 2025/26 is noted

findings.headline: Independent property review identified 16 recommendations, seven rated critical, one critical still outstanding
findings.detail: The paper says the Council has set up arrangements to oversee implementation, but one critical recommendation on reconciling property asset information remains outstanding. The auditor says implementation tracking does not yet give full assurance that all critical recommendations have been addressed.
findings.matters: A finance director or lender can see the open critical items on a property portfolio before its responsibilities transfer to West Surrey Council.
findings.quote: identified 16 recommendations, including seven rated as critical.

findings.headline: Internal audit gives Substantial Assurance opinion across all 9 completed reviews
findings.detail: The paper says the Head of Internal Audit opinion for 2025/26 was given by the Deputy Head of SIAP, which the auditor says broadly aligns with reasonable assurance. It notes the Internal Audit function was outsourced to Southern Internal Audit Partnership during the year.
findings.matters: A finance officer at another council can compare an internal audit assurance outcome, and a lender can see the reported strength of internal control.
findings.figures: 9 completed reviews, all rated Substantial Assurance
findings.quote: The result was a Substantial Assurance Opinion, with all 9 completed reviews achieving this rating.
